item.description:
A sweep for bugs that hadn't bitten anyone yet, 47 of them. The ones you might have met:
- **Your newer passwords stay.** Importing again from another browser no longer puts its older passwords and sign-in cookies over the ones you changed in Changmun. Logins on different ports of one host stay apart, and a two-step sign-in updates your account instead of saving a nameless one. - **Nothing is wiped by a damaged file.** If chat history or archived tabs can't be read, the file is kept aside instead of being written over with an empty one. Saving a page with a long Korean title works, and downloading over an existing file keeps it until the new one is whole. - **Videos and pages stay put.** A paused picture-in-picture video is no longer put to sleep, a page in full screen can't be taken by the AI, a page whose process crashed on its first load loads again, and sign-in pop-ups from the preview card finish. - **Tabs where you left them.** Undoing "close all in group" or a tidy brings tabs back in order, a tab whose bookmark was deleted or moved to another space's favorites stays in the list, and private windows can't save to your bookmarks. - **Smoother start and quit.** Changmun no longer waits on the Safari extension list at launch, ends Claude Code before it quits, and won't wake a tab you closed while it was asking. - **Command line and agents.** `changmun` rejects arguments a command doesn't take, finds and restarts the app after a crash, and the MCP bridge keeps each connection's calls in order and answers pings right away. - **Ranges in AI answers read right.** "3~5" and "10~20" no longer turn the words between them into strikethrough; only ~~two tildes~~ strike through.

- **No more white page after full-screen video.** Leaving a video's full screen (YouTube's f key, for one) could leave the page blank and white until something else happened. Changmun redrew the tab while the video was full screen and lost the spot the page had to come back to. It now leaves the page alone during full screen and puts it back in place when you leave it.

- **Translation tries the other engine.** On some Macs, the translation engine macOS reports as ready refuses to translate. When one engine turns down the whole page, Changmun now tries the other one, then the system's default, before giving up. If macOS's translation doesn't respond at all, it says so and points to Translation Languages in System Settings. - **A record of why a translation failed.** Changmun notes in the system log which languages and engines it tried and what macOS answered, never the page's text or address. If a page still won't translate, run `log show --last 10m --style compact --predicate 'subsystem == "io.github.namekun.Changmun" AND category == "translation"'` in Terminal and send the output along with your report.

- **The loading bar keeps clear of the address.** It still touched letters like g and p at the bottom of the address bar. Loading now shows as a thin line along the top edge of the page, in every toolbar layout.

- **The loading bar sits on the address bar's edge.** It used to float just under the address text and touch letters like g and p. It now runs along the bottom edge of the address bar, rounded with it. - **The command bar and page previews open over the page.** They're centred on the page instead of the window, so they no longer cover the sidebar. - **Orange text you can read in light mode.** Errors, approval questions and "no results" use a darker orange in light mode. - **Small fixes.** The save-login bar shortens the user name before the site name, and the list in onboarding lines up with its buttons.

- **Errors that say what to do.** Not logged in to Claude Code, out of usage, network or server trouble: the panel says which in plain words and offers Try Again. - **Chat history.** Finished chats stay on this Mac and can be read again from the clock button. They're read-only, private windows are never recorded, typed text and address data are trimmed before saving, and you can turn it off in Settings › AI. - **Better answers.** Code blocks, lists and tables render properly, with copy buttons. Links show where they really go, and after a chat has read other sites, opening a link asks first. Long tasks fold into "N steps" with a summary of the tabs opened and closed, and tabs the AI closed can be reopened. - **Easier to drive.** The tab the AI sees shows as a chip; type @ to attach another. ⌘E jumps to the panel, Esc stops, ↑ brings back your last message. Drag the panel's edge to resize it, pick the model from the chip under the box, get suggestions that fit the page, and choose Ask AI About Selection from a page's context menu. - **Questions in the panel.** The AI's questions appear as cards above the box instead of covering the window: Return or Esc says no, ⌘Return allows once, ⌥⌘Return allows that site for the chat. Allow keys only work inside the panel and after a short pause. Paying, deleting and signing in still ask in a window sheet. The panel's head shows which sites the chat has read, and you can take back a site you allowed. - **Images.** Attach a screenshot of the page, or drop or paste up to four images; they're resized and stripped of location data. Images count as something the AI read, so what it does next is asked about.
- **An even address bar.** There was more room above the address bar than below it. It now has the same space on both sides, the bar is a little shorter, and the window buttons sit level with it.

- **The page reaches the edges of the window.** The page used to sit on a card with a gap above, below and to the right of it, which showed as an empty band, most of all on a tall screen. It now runs to the window's top, bottom and right edge, and the AI panel does too, with a thin line between them. With the sidebar hidden or in focus mode, the page fills the whole window.

- **Translation works with the languages you downloaded.** Changmun asked you to download a language even after you had: macOS has a fast and a high-quality translation engine, and Changmun only looked for the fast one. It now uses whichever you have. Text it can't translate stays as it was instead of stopping the whole page, and if nothing could be translated, it says so instead of doing nothing. - **A headless Changmun for your agents.** `changmun headless start` runs a separate, invisible Changmun with its own empty profile, and `changmun --headless …` or `changmun --mcp --headless` (for Claude Code) points at it. It doesn't stop to ask before each step, so it refuses anything that can't be undone, like paying, sending, posting or deleting. Your own browser, its logins and its passwords stay out of it. See `changmun help`.

- **Changmun tells you whether its AI can run.** The last step of onboarding, and the AI panel until you first use it, now say whether Claude Code is on this Mac. If it isn't, you get a link to it, and a note that you can point Changmun at a copy it didn't find in Settings › AI. Codex, Gemini CLI and opencode are named as coming when they're what your Mac has. Until Claude Code is there, the panel's composer stays off instead of failing when you press Return. - **Fewer "Allow" questions from Claude Code.** An AI connected through MCP, such as a Claude Code session, can now be allowed on a site for the rest of its session, as the AI panel could already. It still asks again after reading another site, and anything that pays, sends, posts or deletes is still asked about every time. Commands from the command line are still asked each time.
